title: Unsafe Code and Span Memory Boundary Violations
platform_conditions: .NET Framework 4.x and modern .NET; stackalloc in nested expressions requires C# 8+ / .NET Core, where the runtime may fall back to heap allocation
security_mechanism: stackalloc allocates on the current thread's stack (about 1 MB by default); a length taken from input can push the stack pointer past the thread stack limit, and StackOverflowException is unrecoverable — the process dies with no catch handler. unsafe blocks plus pointers, Marshal.Copy/PtrToStructure with a length or size that does not match the real buffer, and reinterpretation of struct layouts through Marshal.StructureToPtr corrupt adjacent memory when the declared and actual sizes disagree; a Span<T> built over an external buffer also outlives its owner's lifetime silently.

source_sink_clues.source: Request-declared lengths (Content-Length, protocol size fields), record sizes from binary payloads, and buffer sizes chosen from deserialized data.
source_sink_clues.sink: stackalloc byte[userLength] (or stackalloc Span with input length); Marshal.Copy/Marshal.PtrToStructure with input-derived counts; pointer arithmetic inside unsafe blocks over externally sized buffers

tracking_guards: Check every input-derived stackalloc length is clamped to a small fixed constant (or replaced by a pooled heap allocation); check Marshal operations use sizes derived from Marshal.SizeOf<T> of the same type and lengths validated against the real buffer; check unsafe blocks are confined to reviewed helpers rather than request paths.
not_candidate_when: The stackalloc length is a compile-time constant or clamped to a small constant before allocation, the buffer length is bounded by the transport below the stack limit before the call, or the Marshal size comes from Marshal.SizeOf<T>() on the identical type being copied.
public_references: CWE-119: Improper Restriction of Operations within the Bounds of a Memory Buffer — https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/119.html
